chunks: The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mosuli, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

A rabbi from the rabbis came to the Commander of the Faithful, and said: O Commander of the Faithful, when did your Lord come into existence? He said to him: May your mother mourn you! And when did He not exist that it could be said 'when did He exist'?! My Lord existed before the before, without a before, and He will exist after the after, without an after. There is no limit and no termination to His eternity. All limits are severed from Him, so He is the ultimate end of every end.

key_terms.حبر: Hibr - A rabbi or learned Jewish scholar
key_terms.غاية: Ghayah - Limit, terminus, or ultimate end

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about God's eternal existence when asked by a rabbi?
ai.summary: In a gathering during the month of Sha'ban in 368 AH, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that a Jewish rabbi challenged Imam Ali (AS) about when God came into existence. Imam Ali rebuked the question as fundamentally flawed, since God's existence precedes the very concept of time and transcends all temporal boundaries. This teaching was delivered in a theological-dialectical context where Muslim scholars routinely engaged with scholars of other Abrahamic faiths.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi from Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr al-Bazanti from Abi’l Hasan al-Mosuli from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:

A rabbi from the rabbis came to Amir al-Mu’minin and said: O Amir al-Mu’minin! When did your Lord come into existence? So, he said to him: May your mother mourn for you! When did He not existence so that it could be said “when did He come into existence”?! My Lord existed before the beginning, without a beginning. He will exist after the ending, without an ending. He will not terminate, and there is no conclusion to His eternity. He is severed from termination, so He is the end of every end.
